title: Bathtub Float
prompt_en: **Remove** the purple float from the bathtub.
takeaway: In the counterfactual target, the toy car drops straight into the water once the float is removed. Most models either keep the float or leave the car floating in place.

title: Wine Pour (3× Flow)
prompt_en: **Increase** the wine flow rate to 3× (from 60 to 180 mL/s).
takeaway: In the target video, the heavier pour fills the glass far faster. Several models alter the liquid's color or brightness instead of its volumetric flow.

title: Honey on Toast (Frame 51)
prompt_en: **Remove** the honey on the spoon at frame 51.
takeaway: A later-frame fluid removal: the honey must keep pouring until frame 51, then vanish. Several models either remove it prematurely or leave the stream intact.

title: Wall Clock Zero-G (Frame 24)
prompt_en: **Set** the scene's gravity to zero at frame 24.
takeaway: After impacting the wooden crate, turning off gravity at frame 24 lets the clock rebound and drift upward. Most models keep pulling the clock down to the floor.

title: Domino Chain (Frame 13)
takeaway: Because removal occurs at frame 13 (after contact), the cascade must continue without the first domino. Premature removal stops the chain; failed removal leaves the tile in place.

title: Soccer Ball Midpoint Insert
prompt_en: **Insert** a stationary soccer ball at the midpoint between the two balls.
takeaway: Inserting a third ball intercepts both incoming balls and transfers momentum. Nearly all models struggle to place the ball accurately and simulate the three-body collision.

title: Phone Drop + Pillow
prompt_en: **Insert** a blue-grey pillow on the sofa cushion beneath the falling phone.
takeaway: The falling phone must indent and settle onto the inserted pillow rather than hitting the bare cushion. Most models either omit the pillow or pass the phone straight through it.

title: Beach Ball on Soft Hammock
takeaway: A 10× softer hammock sags deeply under the beach ball's impact instead of bouncing it high. Models rarely adjust the elastic deformation amplitude.

title: Flag in Wind (Frame 49)
prompt_en: **Reduce** the wind speed to 0.25× at frame 49.
takeaway: Once the wind drops at frame 49, the taut cloth loses lift and drapes down along the pole. Only MiniMax H3 captures the post-edit slackening; most models keep flapping steadily.

title: Rubber Duck (No Water)
takeaway: Without buoyancy, the deformable duck falls to the empty pool floor and bounces elastically. Most models fail to remove the pool water or leave the duck hovering.

title: Duck under Sink Stream
prompt_en: **Reduce** the yellow rubber duck's core stiffness to 0.1×.
takeaway: A softer duck compresses and sags noticeably under the faucet stream. Models mostly retain the rigid source pose or recolor the duck.

title: Cotton T-Shirt (No Cushion)
prompt_en: **Remove** the right seat cushion from the sofa.
takeaway: Removing the soft cushion drops the falling T-shirt deeper into the sofa frame with different folds. Several models hallucinate an invisible surface where the cushion used to be.

title: Ball in Mug (+ Water)
prompt_en: **Insert** water into the glass mug so the falling orange ball floats.
takeaway: Adding water makes the buoyant orange ball rise to the surface. Models frequently add liquid appearance while leaving the ball pinned at the bottom.

title: Ball on Ramp (No Sponge)
prompt_en: **Remove** the yellow-and-blue sponge standing against the right cabinet wall.
takeaway: Without the energy-absorbing sponge, the orange ball strikes the bare wall harder and rebounds much farther back up the ramp.

title: Plush Drop (+ Paddle)
prompt_en: **Insert** a table-tennis paddle on top of the large plush toy.
takeaway: Placing a rigid paddle on top of the soft plush changes the bounce trajectory of the falling smaller plush toy.

title: EVA Slippers + Shoe Tray
prompt_en: **Insert** a wooden shoe tray on the floor beside the resting slipper.
takeaway: The falling elastic slipper clips the raised tray rim and deflects away from the resting slipper. Top commercial models insert the tray but only partially capture the contact deflection.
